statement: An accessible finite étale neighbourhood of a section kills a specified cyclic character over every residue field above an ordinary rational point a exactly when the section image avoids the compact union of geometric conjugates of the character-nontrivial elements of the point decomposition group at a. Such a neighbourhood supplies the corresponding canonical new-puncture reciprocity test. Universal existence fails for the genuine point section at3, the added point2, and Q(i)/Q, by real path lifting.
where_proved: sections/D_neighbourhood_residue_extension.tex, D.28; finite fibre stabilizers, compact separation by open subgroups SN, regular-curve residues, section evaluation using D.23, and real finite-cover path lifting
depends_on: SGA1 ExposéV finite étale Galois categories; D.23; D.27; D.6 and D.19 local point/cusp comparison; Colliot-Thelene-Skorobogatov2019 Section1.4.1 and Proposition3.6.1
manuscript_passages: 149; manuscript pp.27-31,62v-63; scans56,59-63,126-127; prompt PartD1-D4 and the proposed neighbourhood route to canonical central-lift values
doubtful_reading: No new manuscript reading. This is an exact conditional cover criterion and a counterexample to a proposed universal shortcut, not a refutation of a section conjecture.
notes: Root and finite_field independently reviewed the complete criterion and real obstruction before integration. Elementwise conjugacy is distinguished from conjugacy of sections on the whole Galois group. The Brauer extension is evaluated using an H2(mu_n) lift; D.23 kills the Picard ambiguity. Pairing support for a fixed character does not establish restricted-product admissibility. The actual point example has canonical class1, so its reciprocity test is zero despite the cover obstruction. Even-character and totally imaginary variants remain unproved; C.7h cannot be applied to an arbitrary single global element. D1-D4 remain unresolved.
